title: What are performance anchors?
seoTitle: Performance Anchors in augo | augo support
description: Performance anchors are the baseline fitness values training zones are calculated from — threshold pace, FTP, LTHR and critical power.
summary: A performance anchor is a baseline fitness value for an athlete — threshold pace, lactate threshold heart rate, FTP or critical power. Zone models are defined as percentages of an anchor, so updating the anchor moves every zone with it.

body.html: A performance anchor is a single baseline number that describes where an athlete’s fitness currently sits. Zones hang off it, so the anchor is the thing you update after a test — not the zones themselves.

The anchor types

  • Threshold pace — shown as mm:ss per kilometre, e.g. 4:15 /km
  • Lactate threshold heart rate — in bpm
  • Functional threshold power — in watts
  • Critical power — in watts
  • Body mass — in kilograms

Why they matter

Because zone models are defined as percentages rather than absolute numbers, updating one anchor after a test recalculates every zone built on it. You don’t re-enter zone boundaries by hand.

Tracking change over time

augo keeps the history, so you can see how an anchor has moved across a season rather than only its current value. That history is often a more honest read on whether a block worked than any single session was.

faqs.question: What is a performance anchor?
faqs.answer: A baseline fitness value — threshold pace, lactate threshold heart rate, FTP, critical power or body mass — that training zones are calculated as percentages of.

faqs.question: Do I have to update zones after a test?
faqs.answer: No. Update the anchor and every zone model built on it recalculates automatically.

faqs.question: Does augo keep a history of anchors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Previous values are retained, so you can see how an athlete’s threshold has changed over a season.
